text:
Good evening, Burlington. We're finishing a warm, bright October day in the mid 60s, and with sunset coming at 5:46 it should be a pretty one. The south wind is the only catch. Gusts are running close to 30 mph, so hold onto your hat on the walk home.

A cold front slides through tonight. There's a slight chance of a few showers between 8 and 10, but the forecasters expect only a couple hundredths of an inch, nowhere near a wetting rain. The European model is wetter than the others, so I'd toss a jacket in the car, but I'd bet on sprinkles at most. It stays mostly cloudy and breezy overnight, with a low around 49.

Tomorrow is the reset. Expect mostly cloudy skies, a high near 56, and a gusty west wind, with gusts up to 28 mph or so. Those dry leaves and breezy conditions raise the fire concern a bit, so go easy with any outdoor burning. Tomorrow night drops to around 34, so think hat and gloves.

Halloween looks great: clear, light wind, a high in the upper 40s, and temperatures sliding into the 30s by trick-or-treat time. Bring layers.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-10-29T19:08:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. Increased fire weather concerns through this weekend.
  2. Mostly dry and seasonable conditions continue through the weekend.
  3. A weak cool front early next week will slow a warming trend during another extended quiet weather period.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 303 PM EDT Thursday... No significant changes
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Breezy winds and lower relative humidity values will lead to increased fire weather concerns over the next few days, especially given the plentiful dry leaves serving as fuel. However, Red Flag conditions are not expected. Wind gusts will generally peak in the 20 to 25 mph range tomorrow, with some higher gusts up to 30 mph possible. The gusts will be relatively uniform, with slightly higher gusts in the higher terrain. Minimum relative humidity values will generally be between 40 to 55 percent tomorrow. Heading into the weekend, minimum relative humidity values should drop into the 30 to 45 percent range, but winds look to be much lighter. A weak front moves through the region later today and tonight, bringing some light rain showers, though a wetting rainfall is not expected. Persistent cloud cover tomorrow outside the far southern Champlain Valley and Lower Connecticut River Valley will help limit concerns a bit. KEY MESSAGE 2: After the warm day today, a cold front comes through tonight and into early Friday. A few showers are possible across northern New York and the higher elevations of northern Vermont but with dry air aloft and weak forcing, they will be brief and only lead to a couple hundreths of an inch of rain locally. The highest amounts are expected in the northern Greens and the Adirondacks. Strong cold air advection will occur tomorrow with clouds in the typical upslope areas. A few lingering sprinkles and flurries will be possible in the higher terrain Friday. Surface high pressure builds overhead into the weekend, leading to mostly sunny skies and moderating temperatures. The Halloween forecast looks great with clear skies, light winds and temperatures quickly dropping from the 50s into the 30s during the evening. However, despite clear skies, any added ambiance from the moon will mostly be missing as it was full a couple days ago and will rise around 10:45 Halloween evening. KEY MESSAGE 3: The weather pattern Monday through Wednesday will be fairly similar to what we have seen recently favoring mostly dry conditions but with no big area of high pressure overhead. Guidance has become a bit more consistent with the idea of another cold front slipping in from the north Monday afternoon or evening. Two of the four (instead of one of four as it was 24 hours ago) ensemble clusters/scenarios indicate this, and consistent with the latest run of the ECMWF now in line with this idea. This boundary will bring chances for very light rain and a cloudier period with reinforcement of seasonably cool air. Chances for appreciable rain of reaching even 0.1" in the wetter scenarios is only about 15-40% in the Monday night-Tuesday morning period as the boundary sags slowly southward; near the International Border and higher terrain areas are where chances are sharply greater, including about a 70-85% chance of measurable rain. Overall the model spread for high temperatures on Tuesday has decreased a bit, especially for southern port

NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-10-28T22:25:00Z — same caveat): Mild and breezy Thursday, rain overnight — Thursday turns warmer, as a gusty south breeze sends highs to around 70. Expect lots of sunshine through the morning and afternoon. A cold front brings a band of clouds and spotty showers during the evening, lasting into the overnight. Friday turns mostly dry, with only a spot shower leftover. However, expect more clouds than sun with highs falling back to the 50s. Halloween weekend starts bright but cool on Saturday, with highs in the upper 40s. Sunday turns a bit milder, with highs in the mid-50s, as sun mixes with clouds. Most of next week looks mild for early November, with highs pushing past 60 several days in a row. Monday looks brightest, then more clouds and a greater chance for showers arrive by mid to late week.
